nodes.label: Token Lineage and Indexed Intervention Intervals
nodes.statement: A token-preserving intervention series requires one continuous actual bearer lineage and clock, fixed participant/device identity, signature, code, wiring and realization map except for the named intervention, no reset/retraining/copied-run substitution, and explicitly indexed subintervals. Same token means same bearer lineage under controlled local change, not identity of the complete organization across interventions.
nodes.domain: One uninterrupted participant-device episode and its predeclared reversible intervention subintervals.
nodes.scope: One uninterrupted participant-device episode and its predeclared reversible intervention subintervals.
nodes.source_lineage: R166 W1 same-token requirement refined to avoid complete-organization identity across interventions.
nodes.proof: Definition and identity bookkeeping requirement; no actual episode is supplied.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Process lineage can persist while complete microstate and local organization change; cross-subject or reset comparisons do not satisfy the contract.

formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: every admitted intervention subinterval must satisfy all lineage and indexing clauses
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: P, I, Sigma, K, D, rho and each intervention provenance are explicit

nodes.label: Instrumented Anchor–Mediator–Backup–Consumer Architecture
nodes.statement: A prospective non-invasive participant-device loop realizes a report-independent physical anchor r, a logged live controller mediator k, declared backup routes z, and actual consumers u, with independent reversible interventions on r, k and route gates. The operational k is not asserted to be a hidden neural or complete body representation.
nodes.domain: One instrumented participant-device episode with calibrated safe perturbations; no apparatus or participant was tested in R167.
nodes.scope: One instrumented participant-device episode with calibrated safe perturbations; no apparatus or participant was tested in R167.
nodes.source_lineage: Concrete realization proposal for R166 W2-W5 using established intervention and route-audit ideas; no mechanism novelty claim.
nodes.proof: Constructive specification of physically inspectable states, reads, interventions and route gates.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Sensory or motor perturbation alone is not do(k); hidden routes, off-target effects, invalid fidelity or safety failure block the application.

formal_contract_R167.object_domain: one actual instrumented loop with sorted anchor, mediator, backups and consumers
formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: there exists one declared candidate architecture; every named state and route must be physically realized and audited
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: controller state and participant-device process are distinct but nested actual occurrences within P/I
formal_contract_R167.purpose: Give W2-W5 a manipulable same-episode realization without report-defined ownership

nodes.label: Contextual Relevance Under Declared Redundancy
nodes.statement: For a declared finite deterministic Boolean consumer u=f(k,z), k contributes relative to the declared intervention closure iff there exists a backup context z with f(1,z) unequal to f(0,z); k is contextually indispensable iff the inequality holds in every declared context. Contribution and indispensability are distinct.
nodes.domain: All deterministic Boolean functions with one candidate input k and finitely many declared binary backup inputs; executable enumeration covers zero through three backups.
nodes.scope: All deterministic Boolean functions with one candidate input k and finitely many declared binary backup inputs; executable enumeration covers zero through three backups.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary extensional dependence criterion specialized to R166 W5; Boolean function theory is not claimed as new.
nodes.proof: If all controlled contrasts vanish, f is extensionally independent of k; one nonzero contrast is a witness. The checker enumerates 65,812 functions for m=0..3.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: The theorem is relative to declared variables, deterministic Boolean outputs and intervention semantics; it does not establish closure of the real organization.

formal_contract_R167.object_domain: finite declared Boolean consumer and backup context set
formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: for every f and every declared context; relevance is existential and indispensability universal over z
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: one pre-compensation time slice; abstract f requires separate realization in an actual token
formal_contract_R167.purpose: Prevent redundant masking from being mistaken for no installed use

nodes.label: One Active Backup Masks a Real Primary Contribution
nodes.statement: In u=k OR z, changing k while z=1 leaves u unchanged, although changing k while z=0 changes u. Therefore one null mediator cut in an uncontrolled redundant context does not refute installed use of k.
nodes.domain: The declared deterministic binary OR consumer under controlled interventions on k and z.
nodes.scope: The declared deterministic binary OR consumer under controlled interventions on k and z.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary redundancy countermodel specialized to the R166 mediation witness.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: A validated contextual matrix can resolve this declared model; omitted backups remain possible.

formal_contract_R167.object_domain: one Boolean primary and one Boolean backup route
formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: there exists a masking context z=1 and a revealing context z=0
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: same modeled consumer and pre-compensation time slice

nodes.label: Late Recovery Does Not Refute Earlier Primary Use
nodes.statement: For u_t=k_t OR z_t with z_(t+1)=z_t OR cut_t, cutting an initially active k makes the immediate pre-adaptation output differ from baseline but the later compensated output equal baseline. A late endpoint alone therefore does not refute prior installed use.
nodes.domain: The declared two-step deterministic binary compensation model.
nodes.scope: The declared two-step deterministic binary compensation model.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary finite-state countermodel specialized to timing in R166 W4-W5.
nodes.proof: Baseline u0=1; immediate post-cut u0'=0; after z updates to one, u1'=1.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: The model is not asserted as universal physiology; it refutes only the late-null-to-no-prior-use inference.

formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: there exists the stated initial state and cut sequence
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: same bearer lineage but distinct pre-adaptation and post-compensation subintervals
formal_contract_R167.purpose: Require temporal indexing and prevent compensation false negatives

nodes.label: Invalid, Supported, Closure-Refuted, or Unresolved
nodes.statement: For one named candidate: identity, admissibility or fidelity failure yields INVALID_PROTOCOL; a valid pre-compensation contextual contrast yields PRIMARY_USE_SUPPORTED_RELATIVE_TO_CLOSURE; all valid null contrasts yield CANDIDATE_REFUTED_RELATIVE_TO_CLOSURE only with declared route closure and adequate sensitivity; every other case is UNRESOLVED. Compensation is recorded as an additional temporal flag.
nodes.domain: One predeclared operational mediator candidate, declared finite backup closure and predeclared null/sensitivity bounds.
nodes.scope: One predeclared operational mediator candidate, declared finite backup closure and predeclared null/sensitivity bounds.
nodes.source_lineage: R161 bounded three-way decision refined for same-token mediation, redundancy and compensation.
nodes.proof: Priority logic is exhaustively checked over 128 Boolean assignments; empirical clauses remain uninstantiated.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Any omitted route can defeat closure; null without closure/sensitivity is unresolved and never no experience.

formal_contract_R167.object_domain: one candidate and its declared intervention closure
formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: all validity premises precede any support/refutation; refutation universally covers declared contexts only
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: same token lineage with pre-compensation contrasts separated from adapted endpoints
formal_contract_R167.purpose: Preserve falsifiability without overclaiming completeness or no experience

nodes.label: Operational Discharge of W2–W5, Neural and Semantic Claims Open
nodes.statement: If one common actual episode satisfies the grounded selector, typed Anchor–Bind–Use schema, every R166 W1-W6 clause, the R167 token-lineage and operational architecture contracts, and closure-relative support, then W2-W5 are operationally discharged for the declared participant-device relation. This does not identify a hidden neural or complete body representation, prove route completeness, derive C1, validate B_min, or make the relation a basal-experience gate.
nodes.domain: One common actual P/I/K/D/rho episode and one declared operational relation satisfying all premises simultaneously.
nodes.scope: One common actual P/I/K/D/rho episode and one declared operational relation satisfying all premises simultaneously.
nodes.source_lineage: Conditional application of R157, R159 and R166 to the new operational architecture and bounded triage.
nodes.proof: Bind every premise to the same actual lineage and indexed subintervals; the operational state/read audit supplies W2-W3, valid local interventions W4, and contextual route discrimination W5, while W1 and W6 remain unchanged.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Failure of any all-of premise blocks the conclusion; C1 transport remains R166/R159 conditional and familiar mineness still requires independent B_min.

formal_contract_R167.object_domain: one actual declared operational body-frame relation
formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: every all-of premise holds simultaneously on the one application; no universal neural or experiential necessity claim
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: same P/I lineage, explicit subintervals, fixed K/D/rho except named interventions; C1 applies tokenwise only where admitted
formal_contract_R167.purpose: Turn the R166 witness sketch into a concrete but strictly bounded application route

rules.statement: Same-lineage bookkeeping, an operationally realized mediator architecture, contextual redundancy criterion, and both false-negative obstructions jointly require the bounded closure-relative status logic.
rules.proof_sketch: Invalid identity/fidelity blocks inference; contextual contrast supports use; redundancy and compensation countermodels block unqualified null inference; only closed, sensitive all-context nulls permit bounded refutation.
